units.rhetorical_move: opens on a superlative crisis and then names the modeling job
units.function: state the scale before the method

original_instantiations: A crisis this large asks for a model that keeps the local conditions in view.
The opening names the scale of the harm and only then the modeling task.

units.source_excerpt: The world is witnessing the largest refugee crisis since the horrors of World War II.
units.reusable_pattern: Name the largest instance of the harm, then say the model has to respect local conditions.
reusable_elements: a modeling task that follows it
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the war or the refugee wording.

units.rhetorical_move: stacks two purposes with and take into the consideration
units.function: pair the system view with the local view

original_instantiations: The writeup pairs a system-wide view with a local one in the same sentence.
Two purposes share one verb and the second keeps its own preposition.

units.source_excerpt: an intricate issue that should embrace the sophistication of social interrelated systems, and take into the consideration of refugee crisis on local conditions
units.reusable_pattern: Give the model two jobs in one sentence, and let the second job keep its own preposition even if the grammar strains.
reusable_elements: a local job with its own preposition
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the refugee or the systems wording.

units.rhetorical_move: walks the work in ordinals: in the first place, after that, next, in addition, as for, finally
units.function: serialize the whole solution as a sequence of moves

features.quantitative_role: names the fit statistic at the end of a stage
features.transition: in the first place / after that / next
original_instantiations: Each stage opens with an ordinal, states the move, and ends on the number that justified keeping it.
The summary is one chain of ordinals rather than a list of findings.

units.source_excerpt: In the first place, we establish a set of metrics
units.reusable_pattern: Carry a long solution as ordinals, each one ending on the number that earned the next stage.
reusable_elements: a result that licenses the next ordinal
prohibited_generalizations: Do not copy the metric or the route wording.

units.rhetorical_move: reports a failed first model and the revision in the same breath
units.function: show the discard before the replacement

original_instantiations: A first pass that misses the data is reported, and the revision follows in the next clause.
The failure is kept visible instead of being smoothed into the final method.

units.source_excerpt: the numerical data is inconsistent with real data. Hence, we adjust our presumptions and revise our model.
units.reusable_pattern: Say the first model missed the data, then say the presumption changed.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the migration or the presumption wording.

units.rhetorical_move: gives the fit as R=0.98 and later R=1, written tight against the number
units.function: anchor a stage on its correlation

original_instantiations: A list of shares is followed at once by the correlation that justified them.
The fit statistic sits in the same sentence as the shares.

units.source_excerpt: whose correlation coefficient with real data R=0.98
units.reusable_pattern: Put the correlation in the same sentence as the shares it defends.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the route shares.

units.rhetorical_move: closes the summary by bounding the model: reliable in small scale, needs advancement for larger
units.function: cap the claim at the scale that was tested

original_instantiations: The closing grants the model the small scale and withholds the large one.
A summary ends by saying where the model stops being reliable.

units.source_excerpt: The model is quite reliable in small scale but still needs advancement for larger and more precise simulation.
units.reusable_pattern: End the summary by granting the model one scale and refusing it the next.
reusable_elements: a larger scale that does not
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the simulation wording.

units.rhetorical_move: opens with a double subject and a verb that agrees with neither cleanly
units.function: name the pressure before the cause

original_instantiations: The background names the pressure on the receiving side before it names the cause.
One sentence carries both the region and the wider scope as subjects.

units.source_excerpt: One of the most stressful and potentially destabilizing social challenges facing Europe, or in a wider scope the whole world is the contemporary massive influx
units.reusable_pattern: Open the background with the pressure on the receiving side, and let the subject sprawl.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the influx wording.

units.rhetorical_move: stacks a ratio, a quote, and an attribution in one sentence
units.function: borrow authority for the scale

features.clause_structure: statistic then quoted judgment then source
original_instantiations: A single ratio is backed by a quoted line and the office that said it.
The scale is given as a fraction of the whole population.

units.source_excerpt: One in every 122 people in the world is currently either a refugee, internally displaced or seeking asylum because the world is a mess
units.reusable_pattern: Support one ratio with a short quoted judgment and name who said it.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the displacement wording.

units.rhetorical_move: leaves a stray comma and a space before thus
units.function: concede the count is smaller than the departures

original_instantiations: A concession arrives after a broken comma and still lands the comparison.
The sentence admits the arrivals are fewer than the departures.

units.source_excerpt: reach safety. , thus the true number of arrivals is a lot smaller than that of originals.
units.reusable_pattern: Keep a concession even when the join before it is broken.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the arrival wording.

units.rhetorical_move: cites a death toll and a grant rate with the source inline
units.function: put the human cost next to the acceptance rate

original_instantiations: A death toll and a low grant rate sit in adjacent sentences.
The cost of the crossing is paired with how few are let in.

units.source_excerpt: more than 3, 695 migrants are reported to have died trying to make the crossing in 2015
units.reusable_pattern: Set the toll of the crossing beside the share of requests that are granted.
reusable_elements: a death toll with a split thousands separator
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the crossing figures.

units.rhetorical_move: lists the work as bullets, each one a we-verb plus a method plus a source
units.function: preview the paper as a sequence of moves

features.clause_structure: we-verb then method then validating source
original_instantiations: Each bullet names a move, the method, and the data that checks it.
The work plan is a stack of bullets rather than a paragraph.

units.source_excerpt: We first elaborate reasonable metrics on various factors that affect the movement
units.reusable_pattern: Preview the paper as bullets, each one a move, a method, and the source that checks it.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the metric wording.

units.rhetorical_move: states the assumption, then gives three reasons joined by besides and thus
units.function: justify a grouping assumption with three grounds

features.clause_structure: assumption then three grounds then thus
original_instantiations: An assumption is followed by three reasons and a thus that calls it pragmatic.
The justification is longer than the assumption.

units.source_excerpt: Thus it is pragmatic to make such an assumption.
units.reusable_pattern: State the assumption, give it three grounds, and close by calling it pragmatic.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the group wording.

units.rhetorical_move: uses that is to say and leave out and take no account of
units.function: say what the assumption drops

original_instantiations: The assumption is restated as two things the model refuses to count.
A restatement names the exclusions rather than the rule.

units.source_excerpt: That is to say, leave out the condition that a unit go back from where it has reached to, and take no account of those who stay halfway.
units.reusable_pattern: Restate an assumption as the two cases it refuses to count.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the return wording.

units.rhetorical_move: defends a constant by warning the problem would be a dead end otherwise
units.function: justify holding parameters fixed

features.clause_structure: list of constants then if-not warning
original_instantiations: A long list of constants is defended by saying the problem ends if they vary.
The warrant is a dead end, not a test.

units.source_excerpt: if not so, the problem would possibly be a dead end.
units.reusable_pattern: Defend a list of constants by saying the problem ends if they are allowed to move.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the parameter list.

units.rhetorical_move: introduces the table as notations and descriptions we define
units.function: claim the symbol list as the authors' own

original_instantiations: The symbol table is introduced as one the authors defined themselves.
The claim of ownership sits in the table title.

units.source_excerpt: Table 1.Notations and Descriptions we define in our model
units.reusable_pattern: Title the symbol table as notations you define, with no space after the number.
reusable_elements: a table number glued to its title
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the symbol names.

units.rhetorical_move: prints symbols with the letters split by spaces
units.function: show a symbol broken by the extractor

original_instantiations: A symbol is printed with spaces inside the word.
The split is consistent across the table.

units.source_excerpt: C onvi
units.reusable_pattern: Expect the symbol names to arrive with spaces inside them.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the symbol.

units.rhetorical_move: defines a node as an abstraction whose trait is the same regardless of the nuance
units.function: collapse a region into one unit

original_instantiations: A node is defined by what it ignores inside its borders.
The definition says the trait holds despite the nuance.

units.source_excerpt: whose trait is assumed to be the same regardless of the nuance within the area
units.reusable_pattern: Define a spatial unit by the variation it refuses to model.
reusable_elements: a trait held flat inside it
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the node wording.

units.rhetorical_move: gives two reasons for the year chosen, for one thing and for another
units.function: justify a data year

original_instantiations: A data year is defended by incompleteness on one side and verification on the other.
Both reasons are given before the choice is treated as settled.

units.source_excerpt: For one thing, most of the data in 2015 is incomplete and for another, the latest complete official statistics is up to first half 2015
units.reusable_pattern: Justify a data year with two reasons, one about gaps and one about what was checked.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the year or the agency names.

units.rhetorical_move: writes so as to say inside a presumption
units.function: restate the direction of movement

original_instantiations: A presumption is restated in plainer words in the same sentence.
The restatement says the movement is toward the nearer center.

units.source_excerpt: so as to say, within the emigration centers in a country, the refugees always head for the regions or centers within a circle area closer to Europe
units.reusable_pattern: Restate a presumption mid-sentence with so as to say.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the route wording.

units.rhetorical_move: reports p greater than 0.05 and R of 0.6543, then says the model does not work
units.function: reject a model on its fit

original_instantiations: Two fit numbers are read out and the model is dropped on the spot.
The rejection names the model as the initial one.

units.source_excerpt: Therefore, our initial model doesn't work well, and we right away modify it.
units.reusable_pattern: Read the fit, say the model fails, and say the fix starts at once.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the correlation value.

units.rhetorical_move: cites the textbook form and then says we revise it
units.function: show the borrowed model before the change

original_instantiations: The textbook form is quoted and then replaced by a weight the authors build.
The revision is announced before the new terms appear.

units.source_excerpt: However, we revise our model by figuring out a comprehensive weight indicator to represent the attraction to people.
units.reusable_pattern: Quote the borrowed form, then say what you put in its place.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the gravity wording.

units.rhetorical_move: says the correlation equals 0.9914 and p equals 0.00001, so the data is valid
units.function: accept a model on its fit

original_instantiations: A correlation and a tiny p are read as enough to call the data valid.
The acceptance is one sentence.

units.source_excerpt: So we think this group of data is valid.
units.reusable_pattern: State the correlation and the p, then say in one clause that the data holds.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the fit values.

units.rhetorical_move: names three lines and says line one and line two coincide
units.function: compare the real, the revised, and the first attempt on one figure

features.clause_structure: three named lines then a judgment
original_instantiations: Three lines are named and the judgment says which two lie together.
The first attempt is kept on the figure so the gain is visible.

units.source_excerpt: Evidently, line1 and line2 coincide with each other well.
units.reusable_pattern: Keep the failed line on the figure and say which two lines lie together.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the route labels.

units.rhetorical_move: says whatever the condition is, the flow still passes three named routes
units.function: recommend where to pre-position from two scenarios

original_instantiations: Two opposite weightings still send people through the same three routes.
The recommendation names the routes rather than the weights.

units.source_excerpt: Because whatever the condition is, there will still be huge number of people travelling through this route
units.reusable_pattern: Name the routes that stay busy under both weightings.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the route names.

units.rhetorical_move: reports seven to one country and fifty-one to another, then says the model cannot illustrate the flow
units.function: admit a failed scale-up with the counts

original_instantiations: Two small counts are given and then the model is said to fail at this scale.
The failure is pinned on a named barrier.

units.source_excerpt: So we find that our model can not illustrate the flow of the refugees well.
units.reusable_pattern: Give the two counts the scale-up produced, then say the model cannot show the flow.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the country names or the counts.

units.rhetorical_move: writes the weight mat change, dropping the y
units.function: say the weight changes as the stock changes

original_instantiations: A change in stock is said to move the weight, and the verb loses a letter.
The cause is named before the change.

units.source_excerpt: the weight mat change from node 1 to node 2 as the population, capacity of refugees and the average available resource may change
units.reusable_pattern: Say the weight moves when the stock moves, and keep the sentence even if a letter drops.
reusable_elements: a cause and a changed weight
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the node numbers.

units.rhetorical_move: says a big capacity steadies the flow and a small one makes it unstable
units.function: state the cobweb result as a contrast

original_instantiations: One capacity steadies the flow and the smaller one destabilizes it.
The contrast is the whole finding.

units.source_excerpt: A large capacity of a node will actually make the flow of refugees through the node stable while a relatively small capacity of the node might cause the flow become more and more unstable
units.reusable_pattern: Contrast a large capacity that steadies the flow with a small one that destabilizes it.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the cobweb wording.

units.rhetorical_move: says the nodes stop one it get saturated, with a missing s and a wrong pronoun
units.function: explain the spillover into illegal movement

original_instantiations: A saturated node is said to shut, and the people left pour into the other nodes.
The grammar slips and the mechanism is still stated.

units.source_excerpt: the node stops working one it get saturated
units.reusable_pattern: Say the node shuts once it is full, and let the grammar slip.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the saturation wording.

units.rhetorical_move: defines a cascading effect as one country's change moving its neighbors
units.function: name a second-order effect

original_instantiations: A term is defined as one change spreading to the neighbors.
The definition is the finding.

units.source_excerpt: there is a cascading effect which refers to the fact that a change in refugee policy of a country will affect the migration flow and the attitude towards refugees of its neighbouring countries
units.reusable_pattern: Name a second-order effect and define it as one change moving the neighbors.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the policy wording.

units.rhetorical_move: gives two bands: within five percent the result moves two, beyond ten it moves more than 4.7
units.function: report sensitivity as two bands

original_instantiations: A small shift and a large shift are each given their own output movement.
The bands are the whole sensitivity claim.

units.source_excerpt: when the capacity changes by a small maigin plus or minus 5 percent, then the result of our model change by plus or minus 2 percent, but when the capacity changes beyond plus or minus 10 percent, then the result will deviate by larger than 4.7 percent
units.reusable_pattern: Report sensitivity as two bands, a small shift with a small movement and a large shift with a larger one.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the percentages.

units.rhetorical_move: says the change in node quantity only affects the initial population, not the final proportions
units.function: bound which output a change can move

features.clause_structure: change then only then but not
original_instantiations: A change is said to move the starting population and to leave the final shares alone.
The sentence separates the output that moves from the one that does not.

units.source_excerpt: the change in node quantity only have effects on the population of initial refugees going on migration but not making big difference on the proportion
units.reusable_pattern: Say which output a change moves and which output it leaves alone.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the route wording.

units.rhetorical_move: says we tend to neglect the impact of certain incidents, then gives the example
units.function: admit a factor the weights ignore

original_instantiations: The weighting is said to neglect some incidents, and one is named.
The admission comes before the example.

units.source_excerpt: when we balance the influences of various factors we tend to neglect the impact of certain incidents
units.reusable_pattern: Admit that the weighting neglects some incidents, then name one.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the weather wording.

units.rhetorical_move: says we find it does not match, so we are sure, so we soon make refinement
units.function: turn a failed model into a reason for the next one

original_instantiations: A mismatch is treated as proof, and the fix follows at once.
Three clauses: it fails, we are sure, we refine.

units.source_excerpt: we find it does not match real data, so we are sure that the migration is not random and we soon make refinement on our model.
units.reusable_pattern: Treat a failed model as the reason you are sure, and say the fix came at once.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the randomness wording.

units.rhetorical_move: says the result was verified by real data, indicating the model does have its value
units.function: claim value from a verification

original_instantiations: A check against real data is turned straight into a claim of value.
The claim uses does have rather than a plain has.

units.source_excerpt: the result has been verified by real data, indicating that our model does have its value.
units.reusable_pattern: Let a check against real data license a claim that the model has value.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the gravity wording.

units.rhetorical_move: says we almost leave out one route, but actually there must be some
units.function: concede a dropped route

original_instantiations: An omission is admitted and the missing flow is asserted anyway.
The concession has no count attached.

units.source_excerpt: so we almost leave out the refugee flow on that route, but actually there must be some
units.reusable_pattern: Admit a route you nearly dropped, and say some flow must use it anyway.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the route name.

units.rhetorical_move: says the distances are straight lines and the barriers were ignored, so there are errors
units.function: concede a geometric shortcut

original_instantiations: A straight-line shortcut is named and the error is owned.
The cause and the error sit in one sentence.

units.source_excerpt: The distances in our model are approximated to be straight lines. We ignore the geological barriers on the routes, so there are some errors
units.reusable_pattern: Name the shortcut, name what it ignores, and own the error.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the distance wording.

units.rhetorical_move: opens with uncontrovertibly and a list of drawbacks
units.function: concede before promising more work

original_instantiations: The section opens by granting the drawbacks and then promising more work.
The opener is a single long adverb.

units.source_excerpt: Uncontrovertibly, there are many drawbacks in our model, such as the incomplete collection of relevant data
units.reusable_pattern: Open the future work by granting the drawbacks in one adverb.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the data wording.

units.rhetorical_move: gives three moves: in the first place, besides, lastly
units.function: serialize the resilience claim

features.transition: in the first place / besides / lastly
original_instantiations: Three ordinals each tie a lever to a benefit.
The resilience claim is a short sequence, not a paragraph.

units.source_excerpt: In the first place, if we increase the capacity of refugees of different nodes according to present condition
units.reusable_pattern: Serialize a resilience claim as three ordinals, each a lever and a benefit.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the capacity wording.

units.rhetorical_move: closes the policy with as a whole and to some extent
units.function: bound the policy claim

original_instantiations: The policy section ends by limiting its own claim.
Two hedges share the closing sentence.

units.source_excerpt: As a whole, our policy can adjust to the current situation to some extent.
units.reusable_pattern: Close a policy section with two hedges in one sentence.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the policy wording.

units.rhetorical_move: opens Dear Sir and piles honored, painstaking, day and night
units.function: set the letter's register above the paper's

features.clause_structure: occasion then our effort then our hope
original_instantiations: The letter opens with the occasion, the effort, and a hope that it helps.
The register is far more formal than the body.

units.source_excerpt: I and my fellow colleagues are honored to engage
units.reusable_pattern: Open a letter with the occasion, the effort, and a hope, in a register above the body.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the commission wording.

units.rhetorical_move: says so we strongly suggest and names three concrete provisions
units.function: land the recommendation

features.clause_structure: mechanism then so we suggest then three provisions
original_instantiations: A mechanism is named and then three provisions are asked for.
The suggestion is marked as strong.

units.source_excerpt: So we strongly suggest that the humanitarian response and longer term accommodation, resources and services should be in abundance.
units.reusable_pattern: Name the mechanism, then strongly suggest a small set of provisions.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the provision list.

units.rhetorical_move: closes with an example to follow and a wide comma before the sign-off
units.function: end by pointing at one working case

original_instantiations: The letter ends by pointing at one case and asking others to copy it.
The sign-off uses a wide comma.

units.source_excerpt: we highly recommend that other organizations follow the example
units.reusable_pattern: End a letter by naming one working case and asking others to follow it.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the agency name.

units.rhetorical_move: prints the links with a space before every dot
units.function: give the source as a spaced url

original_instantiations: A reference gives the title and then a url with a space before each dot.
The spacing is the whole habit.

units.source_excerpt: http://www. bbc. com/
units.reusable_pattern: Print a url with a space before each dot.
reusable_elements: a url with spaces before the dots
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the titles.
